record.original_question: When a smooth convex closed curve is approximated by n-gons and the quality of approximation is measured by the area of the symmetric difference, is the resulting function of n related to some billiard-like dynamical system?

evidence.quote: Approximating a convex curve by polygons with respect to the symmetric differ- ence.A popular topic in convex geometry is the approximation of smooth convex closed curves by polygons, see [63]. The quality of approximation byn-gons may be measured by the difference of perimeters or areas, and the polygons may be inscribed or circumscribed. This leads to four functions ofn, and these four functions correspond to the minimal ac- tions of four billiards: the conventional, Birkhoff, billiards, the outer billiards, the symplectic billiards, and the outer length billiards (see [11, 24] about these lesser studied billiards). Consider the approximation of an oval byn-gons where the quality of approximation is measured by the area of the symmetric difference. Problem:is the resulting function ofnrelated to some billiard-like dynamical system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma$ be a smooth strictly convex closed curve in the plane (an oval), bounding a convex region $K$. For each integer $n \geq 3$, define
$$f(n) = \min_{P} \operatorname{area}(K \triangle P),$$
where the minimum is taken over all convex $n$-gons $P$ (one may consider separately the inscribed case $P \subset K$, the circumscribed case $K \subset P$, or the unrestricted case), and $K \triangle P = (K \setminus P) \cup (P \setminus K)$ denotes the symmetric difference.

It is known that the analogous minimal-approximation functions in which the deviation between $K$ and $P$ is measured by the difference of perimeters or by the difference of areas (in the inscribed or circumscribed setting) are realized as the minimal actions (with respect to a generating function) of four billiard-like dynamical systems on the boundary $\gamma$: the classical Birkhoff billiard, the outer billiard, the symplectic billiard, and the outer length billiard. Each of these is a twist map of an annulus whose generating function corresponds, respectively, to inscribed perimeter, circumscribed perimeter, inscribed area, and circumscribed area, and whose minimal $n$-periodic action recovers the corresponding approximation function.

Problem: Determine whether the function $f(n)$, measuring the optimal area of the symmetric difference between $K$ and an $n$-gon, can likewise be realized as the minimal $n$-periodic action of some billiard-like dynamical system on $\gamma$ (i.e., a twist map generated by an appropriate geometric generating function on pairs or tuples of points of $\gamma$). If so, describe such a system explicitly; if not, prove that no such system exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the four known correspondences between polygonal approximation of ovals (perimeter/area, inscribed/circumscribed) and the Birkhoff, outer, symplectic, and outer length billiards, but no source identifies a billiard-like dynamical system whose minimal action equals the optimal symmetric-difference area approximation. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Introducing symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Symplectic billiards use symplectic area as generating function, giving a billiard-like system whose action relates to area-based polygon approximation of convex curves.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the existence of the four billiard-like systems (Birkhoff, outer, symplectic, outer length) tied to perimeter/area approximation, with no mention of a system for symmetric-difference area.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (R. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of billiard systems including Birkhoff and outer billiards.
status_evidence.claim: No billiard-like system is known to govern symmetric-difference approximation of ovals by n-gons.
